term: complete cause of an object's existence
definition: Under Rutten's interpretation G.edge c e means c brings e into existence as its complete cause. Several partial contributors jointly form one sum-cause, rather than each being that complete cause. The source separately requires one INCOMING complete cause per effect; it permits one cause to have many effects.
note: Graph.edge is still mathematically primitive: the name certifies no real causal role. Ordinary production suggests the interpretation, but no independently established physical example of the ENTIRE atomicity/complete-cause/nonoverlap/fusion profile is supplied here; the two-object model is only formal. Complete production differs from constitutive parthood, partial enabling contribution, temporal precedence and generic grounds. Nonoverlap/activity/unique-cause are separate policies, not laws inserted into Graph. No causal transitivity or WF is assumed. In particular R⊆Ground does not lift an uncaused R-source into a grounding root; Ground⊆R, contingent-R-causation or another faithful dictionary would need independent defense.

formal_gap.meaning: Regress.Graph.edge c e is a bare directed edge of the analyst's structural regress schema (#412), from an upstream relatum to its dependent. Under Rutten's interpretation, the one this DEF records, it says that c brings e into existence as its complete cause; several partial contributors jointly form one sum-cause.
formal_gap.examples_unavailable: No independently established physical example of the whole atomicity, complete-cause, nonoverlap and fusion profile is supplied; the two-object model is only formal. Ordinary production suggests the interpretation without instantiating the full profile.
exclusions: Constitutive parthood, partial enabling contribution, temporal precedence and generic grounds (DISAMB-COMPLETE-CAUSE-PARTIAL-GROUND).
Each of several partial contributors taken alone: they form one sum-cause.
open_obligations: The name certifies no real causal role; the edge is mathematically primitive.
One incoming complete cause per effect, nonoverlap and activity are separate policies, not laws of the graph; no transitivity or well-foundedness is assumed.
A causal-to-grounding dictionary (R ⊆ Ground, Ground ⊆ R or another) would need independent defense; R ⊆ Ground does not lift an uncaused source into a grounding root.
No formalization candidate: the graph is a parameter of the schema.
